title: [YouPass Collect] - Film Releases and Ticket Sales in 1996 and 2000
prompt: The graphs below show the total percentage of films released and the total percentage of ticket sales in 1996 and 2000 in a country. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar charts compare the proportion of films released and cinema ticket sales across four genres in 1996 and 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the majority of genres witnessed an increase in both film production and ticket sales over this period, with the notable exception of romance films, whose sales declined. Additionally, while drama represented the highest percentage of releases in both years, comedy consistently attracted the most cinema-goers.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the two dominant genres, in 1996, drama accounted for 27% of all releases, significantly higher than comedy at 20%. In terms of ticket sales, however, the pattern was reversed, with comedy leading at 20% compared to drama's 16%. By 2000, drama releases had surged to 35%, an increase of 8 percentage points, while its sales rose only marginally to 17%. Similarly, comedy releases grew to 25%, and its ticket sales climbed to 23%, maintaining its position as the most popular genre among audiences.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining categories, fantasy and romance films made up 12% and 6% of releases respectively in 1996, while their ticket sales stood at 3% and 5%. Over the following four years, fantasy releases increased to 16%, and notably, its sales more than doubled to 7%. In contrast, romance film production remained unchanged at 6%, but its ticket sales fell by 3 percentage points to just 2% in 2000.
